item.text:
Use a small “checkpoint branch” workflow:

```bash
git status
git checkout -b experiment/my-change
git add <mission-files> <source-files>
git commit -m "Working baseline before experiment"
```

Then experiment freely. If things go badly, you can return to the baseline with:

```bash
git reset --hard HEAD
```

or go back to the original branch:

```bash
git checkout main
```

If you already have uncommitted work that you are not ready to commit, use:

```bash
git stash push -m "baseline before experiment"
```

but a real commit on a temporary branch is usually clearer and safer.

Be careful not to treat generated/runtime files as source. In MOOS-IvP-style work, avoid committing things like:

```text
MOOSLog_*/
LOG_*/
*.alog
*.blog
*.ylog
*.slog
*.xlog
*.klog
build/
CMakeFiles/
CMakeCache.txt
bin/ generated by builds
lib/ generated by builds
```

Mission/source files worth preserving are usually things like:

```text
*.moos
*.bhv
*.sh
*.cpp
*.h
CMakeLists.txt
```

Rule of thumb: commit hand-edited mission configs, behavior files, scripts, and source code; ignore logs, build products, temporary outputs, and generated binaries.
